summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Expanded the direct public-company universe around housing repair, rental operations, property services, title/escrow, warranty, and dispatch rails. The strongest direct exposures are not homebuilders but workflow networks: home-warranty contractor dispatch, property-management SaaS, title/settlement rails, and home-services data/software tied to moving, inspection, insurance, and warranty events. This pass emphasizes USD 300M-10B names and avoids mega-cap housing proxies. Expanded the node toward scarce service rails rather than homebuilders: contractor dispatch/workflow software, home-warranty repair networks, property-management operating systems, and regulated title/escrow/data infrastructure. The underfollowed lane is strongest where local contractor capacity, embedded workflow data, or compliance-heavy transaction processes create switching costs. Current pass is research-only and does not imply any trading recommendation. Expanded the housing-services node through an underfollowed lens. The strongest fit is not homebuilders or mortgage lenders, but companies embedded in repair dispatch, rental-property operating systems, title/escrow transaction rails, and repair/remodel distribution. Four candidates were kept: two mid-cap platform/rail names, one title/escrow transaction name, and one small-cap distributor that is more cyclical but closer to repair/remodel supply flow. No recommendation is implied. Expanded the underfollowed lane around housing-service rails rather than homebuilders or big-box retail.
